Definition: to debar (negatively or positively) from benefit or injury
BiblicalUsage: mânaʻ means to withhold or hold back, for good or for ill. In Proverbs 3:27 the command is to withhold not good from those to whom it is due, and in 1 Samuel 25:26 Abigail tells David the LORD has withholden him from shedding blood. In Jeremiah 31:16 God tells His people to refrain their voice from weeping, and in Psalms 84:11 He promises no good thing will He withhold from those who walk uprightly. The same withholding can be sin, mercy, or promise.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mânaʻ teaches me that God withholds only what would harm me and never what I truly need. I hold that His withholding is love, and my withholding of good from others is sin.
